requirements.evidence: app/Models/Entity.php:23-54 (slug route key, memberships(), many-to-many users(), owner() hasOne filtered on role); app/Models/EntityMembership.php:26 (role cast), :50-70 (owner/admin/employee scopes); app/Models/UserRole.php:7-16; app/Models/User.php:38-59 (memberships/entities/membershipFor); database/migrations/2026_10_29_081655_create_entities_table.php:14-21 (slug, timestamps, softDeletes, entities_slug_unique); database/migrations/2026_10_29_081656_create_entity_memberships_table.php:16-29 (cascading FKs, role default 'employee', stored generated owner_seq, entity_memberships_entity_user_unique, entity_memberships_one_owner); app/Policies/EntityPolicy.php:14-57 and app/Policies/EntityMembershipPolicy.php:14-48 implement every stated rule (create true, member view, owner/admin update/delete, owner-only settings, owner membership never deletable, self-removal, owner/admin delete others); docs/database-schema.md:93,166-167 replaces the old owner_membership_id FK with the owner_seq design.

conventions.evidence: Authorization lives in app/Policies only (no gates/checks elsewhere); EntityPolicy.php and EntityMembershipPolicy.php are argument-less as required and auto-discovered (tests/Feature/EntityPolicyTest.php:78-89); deliberate mass-assignment lists via #[Fillable] matching the existing User model style (app/Models/Entity.php:14, app/Models/EntityMembership.php:12); both migrations are timestamped, artisan-shaped files with reversible down() (…create_entities_table.php:28, …create_entity_memberships_table.php:36); docs kept in sync as the task demands (docs/database-schema.md, docs/README.md:12) plus a CHANGELOG entry (CHANGELOG.md:9); PHPDoc on every public method and relation.

security.evidence: Every ability is decided server-side from the authenticated user's own membership, scoped to the target entity: EntityPolicy.php:22 (view), :30/:38 (update/delete via manages()), :46 (manageSettings), EntityMembershipPolicy.php:16 (view), :22 (assignRole), :31-41 (delete); no client-supplied identifiers are trusted; owner_seq is deliberately not fillable (app/Models/EntityMembership.php:12) so the database-only invariant cannot be mass-assigned; no views, unescaped output, secrets or raw input handling in the diff.

tests.evidence: tests/Feature/EntityDataModelTest.php:1-216 covers columns, indexes, factory states, the generated-column constraints (second owner rejected, promotion rejected, owners across entities allowed, unlimited non-owners), relations and cascade deletes; EntityPolicyTest.php and EntityMembershipPolicyTest.php cover allow and deny paths for all abilities and gate discovery. The only weakness is that the index assertion uses SQLite-only PRAGMA at EntityDataModelTest.php:37-46, so MariaDB (explicitly required by the task) is never exercised, and the documented 'memberships survive entity soft delete' behaviour (docs/database-schema.md:166) has no test.

simplicity.evidence: Minimum Eloquent API: plain relations plus three local scopes (app/Models/EntityMembership.php:50-70), two compact migrations, two small policies; no service/repository layer, no speculative helpers, factories reuse fake()/Str only. Minor duplication: the same private manages() helper is repeated in EntityPolicy.php:51 and EntityMembershipPolicy.php:44.

readability.evidence: Short focused methods with docblocks explaining each rule (EntityPolicy.php:19-21, EntityMembershipPolicy.php:28-30), consistent naming with the domain (owner_seq, membershipFor, manageable), fully typed return values and generic relation annotations; no dead code, debug output or inconsistent style in any of the seven source files.

scope.evidence: Diff touches only models, enum, policies, the two migrations, factories, three test files, and the docs/CHANGELOG the task explicitly asked to update; no routes, Livewire components, middleware, session handling or other out-of-scope features appear in change.diff.

issues.explanation: The index check reads `PRAGMA index_list`, which is SQLite-only, so it would fail if the suite runs on MariaDB and in any case leaves the task's MariaDB portability claim unverified; a driver-agnostic assertion (e.g. Schema::getIndexes) would cover both.
The docs state that membership rows survive an entity soft delete, but no test asserts that entity->delete() leaves the memberships intact (only forceDelete cascade is tested).
The identical owner/admin check (and its per-call membershipFor query) is duplicated in both policies; a small shared private helper would remove the copy without introducing a service layer.

review.summary: The change implements the entity/membership persistence, Eloquent models, factories, UserRole enum and both policies exactly as specified, including the portable DB-enforced single-owner invariant and the required docs update. Code is small, idiomatic and thoroughly tested across allow and deny paths. The only notable weakness is a SQLite-specific index assertion that leaves MariaDB portability untested, so it is approved with minor nits.
